title_en: Pokémon TCG 30th Anniversary Celebration Sealed Booster Bundles Are Back In Stock at Amazon, but You Can Find Better Prices By Shopping Around
summary_en: Amazon has recently restocked its allocation of Pokémon TCG's 30th Celebration boosters, but prices have skyrocketed to all-new highs.
body_en:
Amazon has recently restocked its allocation of Pokémon TCG's 30th Celebration Booster Bundles , which are currently available for $99. But is it the best deal going right now?
Unfortunately, no, this is still above and beyond MSRP, and considerably more than Amazon was selling the booster bundles for in September ($45).
While TCGplayer is still listing the bundles at over MSRP , it is remarkably better than it was just a few weeks back. There's been a dramatic fall in market value on the 30th Anniversary boosters, dropping 35.43% in just the last month. We were seeing these go for around $120 at the end of September, but you can now pick one up, new and sealed, for about $74 on resale.
It's not great versus the $45 Amazon price we saw last month, but still a lot better than the $99 at Amazon now. I'd expect Amazon to drop their price further in the coming days, in order to shift the new stock allocation, especially since the major retailer does like to try and stick close to market rates when it can.
For $99, you're looking at $16.50 per pack (6 in total). At $74, that brings it down to $12.33 per pack. Still not wonderful, but as I said, not as bad as it could be. If anything, it might be worth holding out in case these drop even further, as I don't expect us trainers will be all too thrilled to be paying $70+ for six boosters.
The 30th anniversary set has been remarkably hard to get hold of ever since preorders went live. The set is now officially available globally, but that doesn't mean the hunt for boosters slows down any time soon.
To nobody’s surprise, the secondary market for the new set is in absolute, unadulterated chaos. Queues have stretched out the IRL doors as long as a Cycling Lane at retailers across the world .
For now, to give you an idea of where the dust is settling, we’ve also recently pulled the median market prices per TCGplayer for the top 10 highest-value cards in the set , so you know what to look out for when ripping packs. See those just below, and good luck!
Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.
You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.
His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides .
